title: Anchorwave deploy escort & incremental nightwatch plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a working plan for the Anchorwave micro-release (model routing + batcher tweak). Focus is on an escorted, incremental push with a dedicated nightwatch window so we can observe tail-latency & KV cache effects. This doc is intentionally terse — it's a field notebook for the deploy conductor + nightwatch crew.

Scope / constraints:
- Applies to hosted API tier + dedicated pools (us-west-2 primary).
- No schema changes or DB migrations — purely routing and serving runtime parameter changes.
- Safe to abort at any ramp step; fallback model variant available (anchorwave-v1 -> anchorwave-stable).

Preflight checklist (to verify before t=0):
- [ ] All PRs merged and green: GH PR#1122 merged and smoke tests pass locally (Samir).
- [ ] Telemetry hooks validated: dd/metric and span names spelled out (Evelyn).
- [ ] Canary cluster up-to-date and half-traffic smoke: /canary/host-report OK.
- [ ] Ops pager / oncall notified and rota posted in #release-ops (Luis).
- [ ] Rollforward & rollback commands documented in runbook and pinned (see SRE-RUNBOOK-ID:rb-77).
- [ ] Run the deploy dry-run script in staging: scripts/deploy/dryrun-anchorwave.sh -> exit 0.
- [ ] Security review thumbs-up for config flags (Tomoko).

Quick deploy cheat-sheet (commands):
- Promote config: infractl promote --env=prod --config=anchorwave-routes:2026-06-0a
- Canary toggle: routingctl set-weight anchorwave-v2 0.03 --target=canary
- Global ramp: routingctl set-weight anchorwave-v2 <pct> --target=prod
- Immediate fallback: routingctl set-weight anchorwave-v2 0 --target=prod && routingctl set-weight anchorwave-stable 1.0
- Observability pull (for quick checks): curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/quick?metric=anchorwave.latency_p95&window=5m"

Incremental rollout calendar (local times = PDT):
- T-2h (18:00): Preflight signoff and final smoke, all hands check-in (30m).
- T-1h (19:00): Start canary promotion -> 3% of production traffic to anchorwave-v2. Nightwatch brief handed to L2.
- T+30m (19:30): Verify p50/p95 and error rates on canary window. If no regressions, proceed.
- T+90m (20:00): Ramp to 10% across a subset of regions (us-west-2 + us-east-1 regional slice).
- T+3h (22:00): Ramp to 30% and enable prefix KV caching for v2 in canary group. Observe cache hit/miss deltas.
- T+6h (01:00): Evaluate overnight telemetry and decide on 60% ramp or hold.
- T+12h (07:00): If everything green, complete to 100% or keep 80% with extended observation.

Nightwatch responsibilities (shifts):
- Primary steward (19:00–23:00): Samir Desai — monitor canary dashboards, triage alerts, coordinate fixes.
- Secondary steward (23:00–03:00): Tomoko Sato — focus on tail-latency, redis pressure, and background batch jobs.
- Coverage lead (03:00–07:00): Evelyn Brooks — config ramp decisions, escalate to SRE if error budget consumed.
- Handoff (07:00): Claire Nguyen — summarize incidents & submit release digest.

Observability & telemetry sampling plan:
- High-frequency sampling for first 6 hours: 100% traces for requests hitting anchorwave-v2; capture slow path (>=300ms) and error traces.
- Metrics to watch (automated alerts):
  * anchorwave.latency.p95 (alert if > 1.5x baseline for 10m)
  * anchorwave.error.rate (alert if > 0.5% absolute increase OR > 2x relative)
  * redis.kvcache.hit_rate (alert if drop > 10% absolute)
  * infra.queue.length (background batchers)
- Quick dashboards: /dash/anchorwave-canary, /dash/anchorwave-kvcache, /dash/infra-queues.
- Sampled logs: capture request/response pairs for 1 in 100 requests, increase to 1 in 20 if p95 rises.

Rollback ladder & decision triggers:
- Soft hold: If any single alert fires (minor threshold), pause ramps for 30m and investigate.
- Rollback step 1: Reduce to previous safe weight (e.g., 10% -> 3%).
- Rollback step 2: If multiple alerts across latency+error triggers or customer-facing errors, immediate full rollback to anchorwave-stable (execute Immediate fallback command).
- Escalation: If rollback fails (routingctl error), open incident in PagerDuty and follow SRE runbook rb-77.

Known risks and mitigation notes:
- Risk: KV cache churn may increase cold-start p95 on first requests. Mitigation: enable warmup scripts on a small percentage before ramp.
- Risk: Bursty background batches could queue up. Mitigation: throttle batcher temporarily via infractl batcher set-rate.
- Risk: Regional hiccups under split traffic. Mitigation: regional ramp gating; do not exceed 10% in any region until 2h stable.

Post-deploy checks (first 24h):
- End-of-night digest: short summary (what went up, total errors, p95 delta, rollback actions) posted to #release-ops by 08:00.
- Customer-impact audit: check CS queue for spikes relating to generation failures.
- Perf sampling: run the perf sweep script and save results to the release artifact store.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- [ ] Confirm warmup script for KV cache (Samir to add to PR).
- [ ] Decide whether to delay global ramp until midnight PST vs immediate morning ramp — tradeoff: visibility vs customer-facing window.
- [ ] Validate that dedicated pools in eu-west-1 are isolated from the canary experiment (Luis).

Action items (owners):
- Samir: finalize GH PR#1122 comments and run staging dry-run (due 2026-06-03 09:00 PDT).
- Evelyn: lock telemetry dashboards and pre-create the alert incident channels (2026-06-04).
- Tomoko: review security flags and confirm no secrets rotated during window (2026-06-05).
- Luis: post oncall rota and ensure backup pager coverage for 02:00–05:00.
- Claire: collect end-of-night digest template and verify linked artifacts list.

Notes / field diary (free-form):
- 2026-06-01 11:02 — quick sketch of ramp timeline. Want to avoid big evening ramp; leaning to slow overnight ramp to catch latent cache effects.
- 2026-06-02 16:41 — Evelyn: added new metric anchorwave.kvcache.evictions; might be noisy but useful for early detection.

If anything urgent: call Samir (pager), DM in #release-ops, and if still unresolved page SRE.

END OF SKETCH — this doc will be iterated as preflight items close. Keep this as the ground truth for the deploy escort team.
